# The question

P.Oxy. 5292 preserves twelve intact trimeters of Sophocles' *Tereus* and
seventeen damaged ones (vv. 13–29). Several restorers have filled the damaged
verses: W. B. Henry, the Stoicheia fill-in model, and judge-steered Markov
walks. Which topics does each restorer put into each lost verse, and does that
differ from what Sophocles writes elsewhere?

# The model

Every lemma of the vocabulary belongs to exactly one of $K$ semantic clusters
(word2vec on the lemmatised Greek corpus, Ward's method, cut at $K = 40$; one
rare-lemma cluster and four function-word clusters dropped, leaving 35). Each
cluster is named by the English glosses of
the two lemmata nearest its centre, for example *wretched-miserable* or
*marriage-bed*. A **document** is $N$ consecutive topic-bearing lemmata of a
stream, and its topic counts are

$$\mathbf n \mid \theta \sim \mathrm{Multinomial}(N, \theta), \qquad
  \theta \sim \mathrm{Dirichlet}(\alpha \mathbf 1).$$

The Dirichlet is conjugate to the multinomial, so the posterior is exact,

$$\theta \mid \mathbf n \sim \mathrm{Dirichlet}(\alpha \mathbf 1 + \mathbf n),$$

and needs no sampler beyond `rgamma`. A **cell** (one lacuna, one restorer) is
the equal mixture of its documents' posteriors: its spread is the spread
between restorations plus the Dirichlet uncertainty of each. Sophocles' extant
trimeters are treated the same way, and a cell is compared with them by
$P(\theta_k^{\text{cell}} > \theta_k^{\text{Soph}})$ over paired draws and by
the lift of the posterior means.

# Data

The dataset `Urdatorn/bsda-miniproject-2026` on the Hugging Face Hub: one bag
of content lemmata per restored verse, the vocabulary with its cluster labels,
and the corpus of the three tragedians. The chunk below downloads the three
files (20 MB) into `data/` the first time the report is knitted.

```{r download}
hub <- "https://huggingface.co/datasets/Urdatorn/bsda-miniproject-2026"
dir.create(params$data, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
for (file_name in c("vocab.json", "corpus.parquet", "imputations.parquet")) {
  local_path <- file.path(params$data, file_name)
  if (!file.exists(local_path)) {
    url <- paste(hub, "resolve/main", file_name, sep = "/")
    download.file(url, local_path, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE)
  }
}
```

```{r data}
vocab <- fromJSON(file.path(params$data, "vocab.json"))
corpus <- read_parquet(file.path(params$data, "corpus.parquet"))
imputations <- read_parquet(file.path(params$data, "imputations.parquet"))

# Every row of corpus and imputations is one bag of lemmata: the lemma
# indices (lemma_idx, counted from 0) and how often each occurs (count).
# This function turns a table of bags into one long vector of lemma indices,
# repeating each index as often as it was counted.
lemma_stream <- function(table) {
  indices <- unlist(table$lemma_idx)
  counts <- unlist(table$count)
  rep(indices, counts)
}

# A lemma index becomes the label of its topic. Lemmata without a topic (NA)
# are dropped: they are not observations of any topic.
topic_stream <- function(lemma_indices) {
  labels <- vocab$cluster_K40[lemma_indices + 1]   # R counts from 1
  labels[!is.na(labels)]
}

# The topics, ordered by how much of the tragic corpus they cover
tragedians <- c("sophocles", "aeschylus", "euripides")
tragic <- filter(corpus, source %in% tragedians)
tragic_topics <- topic_stream(lemma_stream(tragic))
topic_mass <- sort(table(tragic_topics), decreasing = TRUE)
topic_names <- names(topic_mass)
K <- length(topic_names)

cat(K, "topics;", nrow(vocab), "lemmata in the vocabulary,",
    sum(!is.na(vocab$cluster_K40)), "with a topic;",
    nrow(imputations), "restored verses\n")
```

# Documents and the exact posterior

```{r model}
n <- params$n
alpha <- params$alpha
draws <- params$draws
max_docs <- params$max_docs

# Cut a stream of topic labels into documents of exactly n labels each.
# If that gives more than `limit` documents, keep a random sample of them.
make_documents <- function(topic_labels, limit, shuffle = FALSE) {
  if (shuffle) {
    topic_labels <- sample(topic_labels)
  }
  n_documents <- length(topic_labels) %/% n
  documents <- list()
  for (i in seq_len(n_documents)) {
    first <- (i - 1) * n + 1
    last <- i * n
    documents[[i]] <- topic_labels[first:last]
  }
  if (n_documents > limit) {
    keep <- sort(sample(n_documents, limit))
    documents <- documents[keep]
  }
  documents
}

# S draws from a Dirichlet distribution: gamma variables, normalised to sum 1
rdirichlet <- function(S, parameters) {
  gammas <- matrix(rgamma(S * length(parameters), shape = parameters),
                   nrow = S, byrow = TRUE)
  gammas / rowSums(gammas)
}

# The exact posterior of one document: count its labels per topic, add the
# prior, and draw from Dirichlet(alpha + counts).
posterior_draws <- function(document) {
  counts <- tabulate(match(document, topic_names), nbins = K)
  rdirichlet(draws, alpha + counts)
}

# A cell's posterior is the mixture of its documents' posteriors: the draws
# of all its documents, stacked. If a baseline (Sophocles' draws) is given,
# the cell is compared with it draw by draw.
summarise_cell <- function(documents, baseline = NULL) {
  if (length(documents) == 0) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  all_draws <- matrix(0, nrow = draws * length(documents), ncol = K)
  for (i in seq_along(documents)) {
    first <- (i - 1) * draws + 1
    last <- i * draws
    all_draws[first:last, ] <- posterior_draws(documents[[i]])
  }
  result <- list(n_docs = length(documents),
                 mean = colMeans(all_draws),
                 q05 = apply(all_draws, 2, quantile, probs = 0.05),
                 q95 = apply(all_draws, 2, quantile, probs = 0.95),
                 draws = all_draws)
  if (!is.null(baseline)) {
    pick <- sample(nrow(baseline), nrow(all_draws), replace = TRUE)
    paired <- baseline[pick, ]
    result$p_above <- colMeans(all_draws > paired)
    result$lift <- colMeans(all_draws) / colMeans(baseline)
  }
  result
}
```

```{r cells}
# Sophocles' extant trimeters are the baseline
sophocles <- filter(corpus, source == "sophocles")
sophocles_documents <- make_documents(topic_stream(lemma_stream(sophocles)),
                                      limit = 4 * max_docs)
baseline <- summarise_cell(sophocles_documents)

# Only untilted restorations are used. The tilt flag is empty (NA) for
# Stoicheia and the candidates, which were never tilted.
untilted <- filter(imputations, !coalesce(style_tilted, FALSE))

cells <- list()

# The walk passages, pooled over all verses
walk <- filter(untilted, restorer == "walk")
walk_documents <- make_documents(topic_stream(lemma_stream(walk)),
                                 limit = 2 * max_docs)
cells[["walk"]] <- summarise_cell(walk_documents, baseline$draws)

# The papyrus as Henry reads it: the intact verses and his restorations,
# as one document
henry <- filter(corpus, source %in% c("intact", "henry"))
henry <- arrange(henry, line)
henry_document <- list(topic_stream(lemma_stream(henry)))
cells[["henry"]] <- summarise_cell(henry_document, baseline$draws)

# One cell per lacuna and restorer; the fills are shuffled before cutting,
# so that a document mixes restorations rather than following one chain
for (verse_number in 13:29) {
  for (restorer_name in c("stoicheia", "candidates", "walk")) {
    fills <- filter(untilted, verse == verse_number,
                    restorer == restorer_name)
    fill_documents <- make_documents(topic_stream(lemma_stream(fills)),
                                     limit = max_docs, shuffle = TRUE)
    cell_name <- paste(verse_number, restorer_name)
    cells[[cell_name]] <- summarise_cell(fill_documents, baseline$draws)
  }
}

# One row per cell and topic, saved as the model's table
rows <- NULL
for (cell_name in names(cells)) {
  cell <- cells[[cell_name]]
  if (is.null(cell)) {
    next
  }
  cell_rows <- data.frame(cell = cell_name,
                          topic = topic_names,
                          n_docs = cell$n_docs,
                          mean = cell$mean,
                          q05 = cell$q05,
                          q95 = cell$q95,
                          p_above_sophocles = cell$p_above,
                          lift = cell$lift)
  rows <- rbind(rows, cell_rows)
}
for (column in c("mean", "q05", "q95", "p_above_sophocles", "lift")) {
  rows[[column]] <- round(rows[[column]], 4)
}
write.csv(rows, file.path(params$out, "posterior.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

# Sophocles' baseline

```{r baseline, fig.height = 5}
baseline_table <- data.frame(topic = factor(topic_names, rev(topic_names)),
                             mean = baseline$mean)
ggplot(baseline_table, aes(x = topic, y = mean)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "posterior mean of theta",
       title = paste("Sophocles,", baseline$n_docs, "documents")) +
  theme_minimal(9)
```

# Topics raised above Sophocles

Topics with $P(\theta_k^{\text{cell}} > \theta_k^{\text{Soph}}) \ge 0.9$,
with the lift of the posterior mean and the mean itself.

```{r raised, results = "asis"}
raised <- filter(rows, p_above_sophocles >= 0.9)
raised <- arrange(raised, cell, desc(lift))
for (cell_name in unique(raised$cell)) {
  cell_raised <- filter(raised, cell == cell_name)
  items <- sprintf("%s (%.1f×, %.2f)", cell_raised$topic, cell_raised$lift,
                   cell_raised$mean)
  cat("- **", cell_name, "** (", cell_raised$n_docs[1], " documents): ",
      paste(items, collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")
}
```

# Lift of every topic in every cell

```{r heatmap, fig.height = 9}
heat <- rows
heat$cell <- factor(heat$cell, levels = names(cells))
heat$topic <- factor(heat$topic, levels = topic_names)
heat$lift_capped <- pmin(heat$lift, 4)
ggplot(heat, aes(x = cell, y = topic, fill = lift_capped)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradient2(midpoint = 1, low = "steelblue", high = "firebrick",
                       name = "lift\n(capped at 4)") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = "Posterior mean relative to Sophocles") +
  theme_minimal(7) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1))
```

```{r pooled}
pooled <- filter(rows, cell %in% c("walk", "henry"))
pooled <- arrange(pooled, cell, desc(lift))
top_five <- NULL
for (cell_name in c("walk", "henry")) {
  top_five <- rbind(top_five, head(filter(pooled, cell == cell_name), 5))
}
knitr::kable(top_five, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE)
```

# Is the walk's topic profile an artefact of where the walk went?

A reviewer may object that the walk's topics only reflect the region of the
restoration space that the chains happened to visit. Two checks answer that.
First, does the lift of a topic drift as the walk proceeds? The walk is cut
into windows of steps, every window is a cell like any other, and the slope of
its lift against the step is the rate of change. Second, do the 120 chains
agree? Each chain's snapshots form a series of topic shares, and the
Gelman–Rubin $\hat R$ (BDA3 §11.4) compares the spread between chains with the
spread within them: $\hat R$ near 1 means a chain's share does not depend on
which chain it is.

```{r walk_lemmata}
# Every walk row is one restored verse of one snapshot (one chain at one
# step, all 17 verses). Chains run alone have an empty chain number, so
# there the chain set is the chain.
walk$chain_id <- ifelse(is.na(walk$chain), walk$chain_set,
                        paste(walk$chain_set, walk$chain))
walk$snapshot <- paste(walk$chain_id, walk$iteration)

# One long table with one line per topic-bearing lemma of the walk: its
# topic and the row (and so the chain, snapshot and step) it belongs to
row_of_entry <- rep(seq_len(nrow(walk)), lengths(walk$lemma_idx))
row_of_lemma <- rep(row_of_entry, unlist(walk$count))
walk_lemmata <- data.frame(row = row_of_lemma,
                           topic = vocab$cluster_K40[lemma_stream(walk) + 1])
walk_lemmata <- filter(walk_lemmata, !is.na(topic))
walk_lemmata$chain_id <- walk$chain_id[walk_lemmata$row]
walk_lemmata$snapshot <- walk$snapshot[walk_lemmata$row]
walk_lemmata$step <- walk$iteration[walk_lemmata$row]
```

## Drift over the steps

```{r drift}
# The lift of every topic in each window of steps. The window's lemmata are
# cut into documents (shuffled, so a document mixes chains) and compared
# with Sophocles exactly as a lacuna cell is.
lift_in_windows <- function(lemmata, breaks) {
  windows <- NULL
  for (i in seq_len(length(breaks) - 1)) {
    in_window <- lemmata$step > breaks[i] & lemmata$step <= breaks[i + 1]
    documents <- make_documents(lemmata$topic[in_window], limit = max_docs,
                                shuffle = TRUE)
    cell <- summarise_cell(documents, baseline$draws)
    window_rows <- data.frame(step = (breaks[i] + breaks[i + 1]) / 2,
                              topic = topic_names,
                              n_docs = cell$n_docs,
                              lift = cell$lift)
    windows <- rbind(windows, window_rows)
  }
  windows
}

# All chains over their common range, in windows of 250 steps
short_range <- lift_in_windows(walk_lemmata, seq(500, 3000, by = 250))
short_range$chains <- "all 120 chains, steps 525-3000"

# The 24 long chains over their whole run, in windows of 1000 steps
long_lemmata <- filter(walk_lemmata, startsWith(chain_id, "chains_eric_long"))
long_range <- lift_in_windows(long_lemmata, seq(1000, 12000, by = 1000))
long_range$chains <- "24 long chains, steps 1025-12000"

# The rate of change: the slope of lift against the step, per 1000 steps,
# fitted by least squares over the windows of the common range
slopes <- data.frame(topic = topic_names, slope_per_1000 = NA)
for (i in seq_len(K)) {
  topic_windows <- filter(short_range, topic == topic_names[i])
  fit <- lm(lift ~ step, data = topic_windows)
  slopes$slope_per_1000[i] <- coef(fit)[2] * 1000
}
```

```{r drift_plot, fig.height = 4.5}
# The five topics with the steepest slopes are coloured; the rest are grey
steepest <- head(arrange(slopes, desc(abs(slope_per_1000))), 5)$topic
drift <- rbind(short_range, long_range)
drift$chains <- factor(drift$chains, levels = unique(drift$chains))
drift$shown <- ifelse(drift$topic %in% steepest, drift$topic, "other")
ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = filter(drift, shown == "other"),
            aes(x = step, y = lift, group = topic), colour = "grey80") +
  geom_line(data = filter(drift, shown != "other"),
            aes(x = step, y = lift, colour = shown)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~ chains, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "step of the walk", y = "lift against Sophocles", colour = NULL,
       title = "Lift of every topic along the walk") +
  theme_minimal(9)
```

## Agreement between the chains

```{r rhat}
# The share of every topic in every snapshot, among its topic-bearing lemmata
counts <- table(walk_lemmata$snapshot, walk_lemmata$topic)
counts <- counts[, topic_names]
shares <- counts / rowSums(counts)
snapshot_chain <- walk$chain_id[match(rownames(counts), walk$snapshot)]
snapshot_step <- walk$iteration[match(rownames(counts), walk$snapshot)]

# The classic R-hat for chains of equal length: W is the mean within-chain
# variance, B the variance between the chain means scaled by the length
rhat <- function(x, chain) {
  chain_means <- tapply(x, chain, mean)
  chain_vars <- tapply(x, chain, var)
  n <- length(x) / length(chain_means)
  W <- mean(chain_vars)
  B <- n * var(chain_means)
  var_hat <- (n - 1) / n * W + B / n
  sqrt(var_hat / W)
}

# Steps 1025-3000 are covered by every chain with 80 snapshots each
common <- snapshot_step >= 1025 & snapshot_step <= 3000
stability <- data.frame(topic = topic_names, rhat = NA,
                        chain_lift_q05 = NA, chain_lift_q95 = NA)
for (i in seq_len(K)) {
  x <- shares[common, i]
  chain <- snapshot_chain[common]
  stability$rhat[i] <- rhat(x, chain)
  # the lift of each chain on its own, against Sophocles' posterior mean
  chain_lifts <- tapply(x, chain, mean) / baseline$mean[i]
  stability$chain_lift_q05[i] <- quantile(chain_lifts, 0.05)
  stability$chain_lift_q95[i] <- quantile(chain_lifts, 0.95)
}

# One table: the pooled lift of the walk, the drift and the chain agreement
pooled_walk <- filter(rows, cell == "walk")
stability$lift <- pooled_walk$lift[match(stability$topic, pooled_walk$topic)]
stability$slope_per_1000 <- slopes$slope_per_1000
stability <- stability[, c("topic", "lift", "slope_per_1000", "rhat",
                           "chain_lift_q05", "chain_lift_q95")]
stability <- arrange(stability, desc(rhat))
write.csv(stability, file.path(params$out, "walk_stability.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(stability, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r stability_summary, results = "asis"}
steepest_topic <- stability$topic[which.max(abs(stability$slope_per_1000))]
sentence <- paste("Over the common range the median absolute slope is %.3f",
                  "lift units per 1000 steps; the steepest topic, %s, moves",
                  "%.3f per 1000 steps. The largest R-hat is %.2f (%s), the",
                  "next largest %.2f (%s).")
cat(sprintf(sentence, median(abs(stability$slope_per_1000)), steepest_topic,
            max(abs(stability$slope_per_1000)), stability$rhat[1],
            stability$topic[1], stability$rhat[2], stability$topic[2]), "\n")
```

So the walk's topic profile is stationary: no topic drifts by more than a
tenth of a lift unit over the common range, and the long chains hold their
lifts to step 12000. The chains agree on every topic but one. *Sail-sea* has
$\hat R$ far above 1 and chain-level lifts ranging from near zero to several
times Sophocles': some chains sailed into sea vocabulary and stayed there,
others never went. Its raised lift at v. 14 in the walk cell is therefore an
artefact of where those chains went, not a property of the lacuna, and it is
the one walk result that should be discounted. The other raised walk topics,
*good-just* at vv. 17–18, are shared by all chains.
